references.text: The place was called Kibroth-hattaavah (graves of craving) because the people who had craved meat were buried there, as a direct result of the plague described in verse 33.
Psalm 78 describes the same event: God's anger came upon them while the food was still in their mouths, and he struck down the strongest among them.
Refers to Israel's craving in the wilderness and how God gave them what they asked for, but sent a wasting disease upon them.
Moses reminds the people of how they aroused the Lord's anger at Taberah, Massah, and Kibroth-hattaavah.
Paul uses Israel's craving in the wilderness as a warning to Christians in Corinth not to crave evil things as their ancestors did.
Paul warns against grumbling as some of the Israelites did, who were killed by the destroyer - a reference to the plagues in the wilderness.
The book of Hebrews refers to those who sinned in the wilderness and whose bodies fell there, as a warning about the consequences of disobedience.
